definitions.gloss: hearing a hundred times; hearing something many times
definitions.explanation: Hearing about something repeatedly from others rather than experiencing it firsthand. Almost exclusively used in the proverb {百聞|ひゃくぶん}は{一見|いっけん}にしかず (seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times).

examples.japanese: {百聞|ひゃくぶん}は{一見|いっけん}にしかず。
examples.english: Seeing is believing. (Hearing a hundred times is not worth seeing once.)

examples.japanese: {百聞|ひゃくぶん}は{一見|いっけん}にしかずと{言|い}うから、{実際|じっさい}に{見|み}に{行|い}こう。
examples.english: They say seeing is believing, so let's go see it in person.

examples.japanese: {写真|しゃしん}では{伝|つた}わらない。{百聞|ひゃくぶん}は{一見|いっけん}にしかずで、{現地|げんち}に{行|い}ってこそ{分|わ}かるものだ。
examples.english: Photos can't convey it. As the saying goes, seeing is believing — you can only understand by going there yourself.

notes:
Composed of {百|ひゃく} (hundred) and {聞|ぶん} (hearing). Almost always used as part of the proverb {百聞|ひゃくぶん}は{一見|いっけん}にしかず, which comes from the Chinese historian Ban Gu's Book of Han. The equivalent English proverb is "Seeing is believing" or "A picture is worth a thousand words."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {百聞|ひゃくぶん}は{一見|いっけん}にしかず (seeing once is worth more than hearing a hundred times)

NOTE ON USAGE:
{百聞|ひゃくぶん} rarely appears independently outside this proverb. It is included as a dictionary entry because the proverb itself is extremely well-known and frequently used in Japanese.
